name: Jzzhu and Numbers
description: Jzzhu have n non-negative integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . We will call a sequence of indexes i 1 , i 2 , ..., i k (1 ≤ i 1 < i 2 < ... < i k ≤ n ) a group of size k . Jzzhu wonders, how many groups exists such that a i 1 & a i 2 & ... & a i k = 0 (1 ≤ k ≤ n ) ? Help him and print this number modulo 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) . Operation x & y denotes bitwise AND operation of two numbers.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10 6 ) . The second line contains n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (0 ≤ a i ≤ 10 6 ) .
output_specification: Output a single integer representing the number of required groups modulo 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) .
approach_summary: Define state dp[mask][i] capturing the subset of visited/chosen elements. Transition by iterating over valid unset bits in O(2^N × N) time.
